title: Story Foundation Pack
description: The canonical structured foundation for a book project. This is the source of truth. It is managed by the workflow, not directly by the model.

version.description: Integer counter incremented on every merge. Starts at 1.

last_modified.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last merge.

changelog.description: One entry per merge round. Append-only. Never delete entries.

summary.description: Brief summary of what changed in this round.

patches_applied.description: Number of patches applied in this merge.

format.description: Novel, novella, series, short story, etc.

premise.description: One or two sentence distillation of what the story is about.

hook.description: The compelling question or tension that draws a reader in.

world_foundation.description: The parts of the world that actually affect story.

setting_type.description: Secondary world, real-world, historical, near-future, etc.

major_world_rules.description: Rules that constrain or shape what is possible in this world.

power_structures.description: Who has power and how it is organized.

world_conflicts.description: Macro-level tensions in the world beyond the protagonist's story.

secrets.description: World-level secrets or hidden truths that the story may reveal.

story_question.description: The dramatic question the story must answer by its end.

stakes.description: What is lost if the protagonist fails.

hooks.description: Narrative hooks that sustain reader interest across the story.

pressure_points.description: Recurring sources of tension or complication.

internal_need.description: What they actually need, often in conflict with their want.

wound.description: The backstory injury that shapes their behavior.

arc_direction.description: Positive arc, negative arc, flat arc, etc.

voice_notes.description: How this character sounds and thinks on the page.

function.description: What narrative job this character performs.

plot_frame.description: Structural skeleton. Does not need to be complete before drafting can begin, but gaps should be flagged.

beginning_state.description: World and protagonist state at the story's opening.

inciting_incident.description: The event that ruptures the beginning state and forces the story forward.

first_turn.description: The point of no return — protagonist commits to the story's path.

midpoint.description: A major shift in understanding, stakes, or approach at the story's center.

darkest_moment.description: The lowest point. Maximum pressure before the final push.

resolution_shape.description: The general shape of what follows the climax.

set_pieces.description: Significant scenes or sequences already envisioned.

ending_design.description: Explicit ending detail. This section is treated as high priority — a vague ending produces weak writing throughout.

final_image.description: The last image or moment of the story.

relationship_end_states.description: Where each key relationship ends up.

world_state_after.description: What the world looks like after the climax resolves.

required_payoffs.description: Promises made earlier in the story that must be paid off.

emotional_ending_feel.description: The emotional register of the ending — hopeful, bittersweet, tragic, cathartic, etc.

author_preferences.description: Author voice, taste, and hard constraints. This section is critical for Step 3 — it distinguishes the author's voice from generic output.

pov_preference.description: First person, third limited, third omniscient, etc.

prose_register.description: Sparse, dense, lyrical, journalistic, colloquial, etc.

chapter_length_target.description: Approximate target word count per chapter.

explicit_inspirations.description: Specific books whose style is a target reference, not just general taste.

must_include.description: Elements the author insists on having in the story.

must_avoid.description: Elements the author will not include under any circumstances.

content_limits.description: Explicit content ceiling — what the author will not write at all.

trope_targets.description: Tropes the author wants to use deliberately.

trope_avoids.description: Tropes the author explicitly does not want.

non_negotiables.description: Hard constraints that override story logic if there is a conflict.

open_questions.description: Unresolved issues that still need author input. Managed by the workflow, not the model directly.

section.description: Which section of the pack this question pertains to.

completeness_status.description: Readiness assessment per section. Used to gate Step 3. See docs/completeness_criteria.md for scoring rules.

blocking_issues.description: Specific issues preventing advancement to the next stage.

field_status.description: confirmed: author has approved this. tentative: raised but not locked in. unresolved: explicitly unknown. superseded: was once confirmed but has since been replaced — kept for history.

set_in_version.description: Pack version when this value was last set.

readiness_level.description: not_started: no confirmed fields. partial: some confirmed fields but gaps remain. sufficient: enough confirmed content to proceed. locked: author has signed off, do not overwrite.
